newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 3.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 3.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Sportswear maker Adidas AG signs a global market alliance with the National Basketball Association, giving the company licensing rights to sell NBA merchandise in the United States. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Advertising group Leo Burnett launches a new agency in Vienna with Wirz Wien. Fiat will be its first client.(Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Internet ad planning and booking system Plan.NET is now up and running. Advertising agencies can visit the site to investigate current ad placement possibilities on the World Wide Web. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Media giant Bertelsmann and Bavarian tycoon Leo Kirch appear finally set to launch digital television. In a move that breaks a long deadlock, phone giant DeutscheTelekom reaches a deal with broadcaster CLT/Ufa and Kirch ondigital decoders that will make digital TV available to Telekom's 17 cable TV subscribers in Germany within months.(Reuter)

HAMBURG - Kirch Group, which has bought an additional 37.5 percent stake in pay-television broadcaster Premiere, will sell one third of that stake to Bertelsmann affiliate CLT-UFA, Premiere says.(Reuter)

BONN - Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet appoints Klaus-Dieter Scheuerle, a senior post ministry official, to head a new watchdog agency for the telecoms sector after liberalisation on January 1, 1998.(Reuter)

BONN - The biggest German magazines saw a drop in ad revenues during the first half of this year, with the exception of news magazine Focus, says the Association of German Periodical Publishers. (Reuter)

KASSEL - Media authorities in the state of Hesse have issued trial licenses to three digital television providers. In a pilot programme, Kirch-owned station DF1, programming package MultiThematique and pay-TV channel Premiere, can begin digital broadcasting on the cable network there, says the state private broadcasting authority. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
INGOLSTADT - Luxury carmaker Audi AG, a unit of Volkswagen AG, says it is raising annual production of its A3 model by 25,000 vehicles to 125,000.(Reuter)

COLOGNE - The German unit of carmaker Ford plans to return to the black with price cuts and an improved offering of models, Ford-Werke AG chief executive William Boddie says.(Reuter) ***********************************************
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Lucas Mees, president of DDB Northern Europe, will temporarily take control of the company's German operations following the sudden departure of German chief executive Klaus Flettner.(Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Hans Germeraad, chief executive of Initiative Media in Hamburg, will leave the company to sit at the helm of HMS Carat Deutschland in Wiesbaden.(Horizont)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
